## Solution

Let $F$ be the number of freshmen admitted each year (constant in steady state). At the start of each school year, the four classes are populated by the survivors of the previous year's classes:

| Class at year start | Size |
|---|---|
| Freshmen | $F$ (just admitted) |
| Sophomores | $\tfrac{2}{3}F$ (freshmen lose $\tfrac{1}{3}$) |
| Juniors | $\tfrac{2}{3}F - 40$ (sophomores lose $40$) |
| Seniors | $\tfrac{9}{10}\!\left(\tfrac{2}{3}F - 40\right)$ (juniors lose $\tfrac{1}{10}$) |

The college wants the total enrollment at the start of each year to be $3400$:

$$F + \tfrac{2}{3}F + \left(\tfrac{2}{3}F - 40\right) + \tfrac{9}{10}\!\left(\tfrac{2}{3}F - 40\right) = 3400.$$

Expanding the last term: $\tfrac{9}{10}\cdot\tfrac{2}{3}F = \tfrac{3}{5}F$ and $\tfrac{9}{10}\cdot 40 = 36$, so

$$F + \tfrac{4}{3}F - 40 + \tfrac{3}{5}F - 36 = 3400.$$

Combining the $F$-terms over a common denominator of $15$:

$$\frac{15F + 20F + 9F}{15} - 76 = 3400 \;\;\Longrightarrow\;\; \frac{44F}{15} = 3476.$$

Solving:

$$F = \frac{3476 \times 15}{44} = \frac{52140}{44} = 1185.$$

**Verification.** With $F = 1185$:
- Freshmen: $1185$
- Sophomores: $\tfrac{2}{3}(1185) = 790$
- Juniors: $790 - 40 = 750$
- Seniors: $\tfrac{9}{10}(750) = 675$

Total: $1185 + 790 + 750 + 675 = 3400$. ✓

The college needs to admit $\boxed{1185}$ students into the freshman class each year.
